prop: Every observation in this memo was taken against the worktree at /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel, on branch main, clean per `git status --porcelain -b`, at commit 01b140c74882b17ccb157839cf205794a0aaaa49.

The doc comment on `render_facts` in src/compose.rs — "a committed document should not carry `/Users/<someone>/...`" — is false of the artifacts the tool actually produces: three committed memos carry 218, 127 and 145 occurrences of /Users/ or /Volumes/ paths in their rendered markdown, and 448, 275 and 350 in their snapshot directories.

Within a committed snapshot directory, machine-local absolute paths are concentrated almost entirely in facts.jsonl (448 of 448, 273 of 275, 348 of 350 occurrences across the three memos measured); prose.jsonl, targets.jsonl, transplants.jsonl, counters.json, identity.json, pending.json and refusals.log carry none, and claims.jsonl carries 2 in two of the three.

The label and the key are independent fields set at capture and copied verbatim by `mint`: the key is `fs::canonicalize`d (absolute by construction), while a plain `look`'s label is the path exactly as the caller spelled it. Relativizing a label is therefore a change to one expression inside `observe.rs`, and the anchor it would need — `world_root`, resolved from the observed path — is already computed on the same pending entry.

A capture-time label change necessarily changes the pin: `mint` hashes each pending entry's label, world_root, world_state and output, and does not hash the key. The same observation of the same file at the same tree state therefore pins differently before and after such a change.

Keys must remain absolute: `ExtentEntry::censuses` — the predicate behind every `target` declaration — requires `self.key == self.world_root`, comparing the captured key against the captured worktree root. `search_key` exists precisely to reconcile the two tools' spellings of that one absolute directory.

`ExtentEntry` already carries four `#[serde(default)]` fields whose absence is documented as "not recorded" rather than as a default value — `world_root`, `kind`, `out_len` and `matcher` — so adding a fifth to mark "label computed root-relative at capture" extends an established idiom rather than introducing one.

Nothing in tetel recomputes a fact pin or compares one against another: src/facts.rs:556 is the sole computation site; src/evidence.rs:399 and src/query.rs:13 only copy and print it; and the only tests asserting anything about a fact pin (tests/authoring_cli.rs lines 3221-3302) assert relative equality between two pins minted in the same run and hard-code no literal. A pin discontinuity introduced by a capture-time label change therefore breaks no code path and no test on this build.

"Pin" names two unrelated things in this codebase, and only one of them is affected: a fact's content fingerprint (src/facts.rs), and the document-level "at pin `<hash>`" commit id an author writes into a memo's evidence ledger and src/ledger.rs/src/parse.rs parse into a row's `pin` field. A capture-time label change touches the first and not the second.

`snapshot::check` compares a memo's committed bytes against a full re-render of its snapshot (`rendered == memo_source`), so any change to render output reddens `[provenance-drift]` on every committed memo at once. A capture-time label change cannot do this: `render_facts` prints each stored label verbatim, so an unchanged snapshot re-renders byte-identically no matter what a newer build would have captured.

The repository holds exactly 8 committed rendered memos with snapshots, all under docs/design/, and on the build that identifies itself as `tetel 0.1.0 build ac89d5481e9b` every one of them checks at exit 0 with no `provenance-drift` line. The drift baseline this work must not disturb is therefore 0 of 8.

Between 77% and 90% of the absolute paths in a committed memo point inside the repository the memo itself ships in (195/218, 98/127, 119/145 across tet61, tet47 and tet56). Relativizing labels against the worktree root therefore converts the large majority of a memo's machine-local paths into paths a reader who cloned the repository can open, rather than merely shortening them.

Not every absolute path in a rendered memo is a tool-generated label: of the three memos measured, 0, 1 and 4 occurrences fall outside the Facts table, and they are of two kinds — extent labels printed by a second render site (the transplants section's "Donor extent (captured)" line, src/compose.rs:195, which no label mechanism distinguishes from src/compose.rs:293) and author-typed claim propositions, such as tet56's C1 beginning "The tree this memo's observations were taken against is /Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel at HEAD 81137aa...". No capture-time label change can reach the author-typed ones.

An absolute label is structural, not an authoring mistake. Every `look` label is built from the path as the caller spelled it, and the MCP server — through which agents author — documents that every path-taking parameter must be absolute, because a relative one resolves against a server working directory the caller cannot see or set, a failure that has already cost a run. No amount of author care can produce a relative label over MCP.

A `run` observation is not a path observation and must be left alone: its key is the command line itself, not a filesystem path, and its label is `proc: {cmdline} (exit {exit_code})`. Rewriting any part of that argv would make the record state that a command was run which was not run.

The anchor should be `world_root` (the observation's own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), not the memo's directory. `world_root` is resolved at capture from the observed path and is already on the pending entry, whereas the memo's location does not exist until `render --out` — an anchor a capture-time mechanism cannot consult. Empirically the two coincide for the whole committed corpus: across all 8 snapshots every extent entry's world_root is either this repository or the degraded NO_GIT marker, and no committed memo cites a fact taken against a different repository than the one it ships in.

A relativized label is only unambiguous if the reader can tell which tree it is relative to, and a rendered memo does not say: `check` on tet61 emits no row naming the memo's world root, only the standing human-owed header sentence about working-tree states. The root survives in the snapshot's facts.jsonl and, by convention, in the author-typed pin claim — neither of which is a mechanism the tool enforces.

A forgery surface exists and it is in the label, not the key. Measured on the current build: `look <repo>/link/x.txt` through a symlink out of the repo, and `look <repo>/../outside/x.txt`, both store a label textually beginning with the repo root while the file is outside it. In every such case the key — which is canonicalized — is the outside path, and the entry's own world_root is either `no-git-worktree` or the outside file's own repository, never the repository the label appears to sit under.

The relative label must be derived from the canonicalized key against the entry's own world_root, never by stripping a prefix from the caller's spelling. Deriving it from the key makes the escape cases refuse automatically — the key is not under the repo root, so no strip applies and the label stays absolute — whereas a textual strip of the caller's spelling would mint `link/x.txt` for a file outside the repository.

The blast radius is bounded and censused. `PendingEntry` is named in source only by src/pending.rs (definition), src/observe.rs (every construction site) and src/facts.rs (the fold in `mint`); `ExtentEntry` is named only by src/facts.rs, src/scope.rs, src/worldstate.rs, src/targets.rs and src/checks.rs, and by no other file under src/; `render_facts` is defined and used only within src/compose.rs, with a single mention in src/ledger.rs. Every other occurrence of all three across the worktree is committed memo prose or verifier-eval evaluation transcripts, not code.

In an evidence ledger, machine-local paths sit in exactly two places and only one of them can move: across the 8 committed `<memo>.evidence.jsonl` files, 5621 occurrences are in `predicate.extent[]`, which src/evidence.rs builds as `fact.extent.iter().map(|e| e.label.clone())` and which a capture-time label change therefore fixes; 901 are in `predicate.world[].root`, the worktree identity itself; 16 are in a grader's `predicate.note`. No occurrence is in `predicate.source`, `predicate.pin`, `world[].state`, the subject, or any other field.

The contract TET-42 should adopt, per artifact: (1) a rendered memo guarantees that every tool-generated extent label citing a file inside the worktree the observation was taken against is spelled relative to that worktree root, and makes no promise about author-typed text or about `proc:` command lines; (2) an evidence ledger inherits that guarantee for `predicate.extent[]` and explicitly keeps `predicate.world[].root` absolute, because it is the identity of the tree, not a citation into it; (3) a snapshot keeps every `key` absolute and canonical, because `key` is what `ExtentEntry::censuses` compares against `world_root`, and stores the same relativized labels the memo renders. This is deliverable because labels and keys are independent fields, the label is built at capture from a `world_root` already on the pending entry, and the only render sites print stored labels verbatim.

What a committed artifact already survives, and what it does not, are different things. A memo, its evidence ledger and its snapshot copied alone into a fresh git repository at a different absolute path, with an empty state home and no workspaces, already check at exit 0 with no provenance drift — citation ids resolve off-workspace today. What does not survive is a reader's ability to open what a fact opened. Against a clone of this repository at a different absolute path, stripping the worktree prefix from each memo's distinct in-repo absolute paths resolves 32 of 35, 21 of 23 and 32 of 36 to files that exist there; the absolute forms resolve to nothing. A small non-zero residue does not resolve even relativized, and this design did not diagnose it.

Portability, not privacy, is what justifies this change, and privacy must not be promised. After a capture-time label change a committed artifact still carries machine-local paths in author-typed claim propositions, in `proc:` command lines and their keys, in every extent `key`, and in `predicate.world[].root` — 901 occurrences of the last across the eight committed evidence ledgers alone.

At the destination the marker's absence disables a specific use with a cheap remedy, exactly as the donor's fields require: an extent entry with no root-relative marker may not be read as openable against the worktree root, only as spelled by whoever captured it, and the remedy is to look again under the new build — cheap because extent and label are immutable per fact but a new observation of the same file costs one `look`.

Absence of the marker cannot be read as any default value, which is what the donor's "never *zero*" clause demands. An unmarked label is not reliably absolute: the CLI accepts a relative path and the pin tests exercise exactly that (`look f.txt` with the repo as cwd), while the MCP surface requires an absolute one. So the only true reading of an absent marker is "spelled as the caller typed it, with no resolvability guarantee" — not "absolute" and not "relative".

A whole-search record is the one case where the relative form is degenerate: `search_key` stores world_root's own spelling as the key whenever the search root and the worktree root name the same directory — which is precisely the case `ExtentEntry::censuses` requires — so stripping world_root from that key leaves the empty string. The implementation must choose an explicit spelling for the root itself, and the `no-match`/`search` labels additionally interpolate the search root and an exclusion note that enumerates skipped paths in full.

The share of a rendered memo's machine-local path occurrences that the mechanism designed here actually converts — entries whose own world_root resolved to a real repository, whose canonical key sits strictly under it, and which are not `proc:`-exempt — is 93 of 218, 48 of 127 and 75 of 145 across tet61, tet47 and tet56: 38% to 52%, not a large majority. Each such entry is a plain single-file label carrying exactly one path, so converted entries and converted occurrences are the same count. Three exclusions absorb the difference and every one of them is the design's own: `proc:` labels (6, 17, 19 occurrences), an entry whose world marker degraded to `no-git-worktree` (1, 1, 0), and above all the whole-search label whose key equals world_root (113, 51, 38) — the single largest bucket in two of the three memos.

Between 77% and 90% of the absolute paths in a committed memo are textually contained in the repository the memo itself ships in (195/218, 98/127, 119/145 across tet61, tet47 and tet56). That is an upper bound on what any worktree-anchored relativization could reach, not the share this design converts: it counts an occurrence wherever the repository root appears as a prefix, irrespective of whether the entry carrying it has a resolved world_root, has a key strictly under that root, or is `proc:`-exempt. The delivered share, measured by the design's own rule, is C28's.
why: Answers the `qualifies` verdict on C12. The 77-90% figure is correct but measures textual containment, and the design spent it as if it were the delivered share; the claim now says which quantity it is and points at C28 for the other.

prop: The whole-search label is not a corner case and the contract must decide it rather than leave it to the implementer: it carries 113 of tet61's 218, 51 of tet47's 127 and 38 of tet56's 145 machine-local path occurrences — more than the plain file labels in two of the three memos — and all 113, all 51 and all 38 name paths under the very worktree the memo ships in. The decision: spell a search root that equals world_root as `.`, and apply the same key-derived rule to each path the exclusion note enumerates — relative to world_root when it lies under it, absolute otherwise. This preserves the note's stated purpose, since distinct paths stay distinct under a common prefix strip and therefore still pin differently. Taken with C28, deciding this converts 206 of 218, 99 of 127 and 113 of 145 rather than 93, 48 and 75.
why: Answers the `qualifies` verdict on C27. Measured, this label is the largest single carrier of machine-local paths in two of three memos, so leaving its spelling to the implementer leaves more than half the benefit undecided. Promoted from a degenerate-case footnote to a stated decision, with the exclusion note's enumerated paths brought inside the rule.

prop: The relative label must be derived from the canonicalized key against the entry's own `world_root`, AND minted only when the caller's own spelling lies under that same `world_root`. Two conditions, because each defeats a different attack and neither defeats both. Deriving from the key rather than by stripping a prefix off the caller's spelling defeats the escape into a non-repository: `look <repo>/link/x.txt` through a symlink out of the tree, and `look <repo>/../outside/x.txt`, both carry a key that is not under the repository root, so no strip applies and the label stays absolute, where a textual strip would have minted `link/x.txt`. But the key-derived rule alone does not defeat the escape into a *different* repository, and that case is reachable with an ordinary symlink. Constructed and captured on the release build: `look .../outer/link/x.txt`, where `outer/link` is a committed symlink to a separate repository `otherrepo`, mints key `.../otherrepo/x.txt` and `world_root` `.../otherrepo`, because `Session::for_path` canonicalizes the containing directory before asking git. The key is strictly under that entry's own world_root, so a key-only rule mints the relative label `x.txt` — not absolute and not a refusal — and `x.txt` resolves in the shipping worktree `outer` to a file that exists there holding "OUTER x" against the observed "OTHER FILE". The second condition catches exactly that: the caller's spelling `.../outer/link/x.txt` does not lie under `world_root` `.../otherrepo`, whereas in the control observation `look .../outer/README.md` the key, the label and the world_root all agree. Both operands are already on the pending entry, so this adds a second comparison rather than a new mechanism, and it costs nothing on any observation that did not traverse out of the tree the caller was working in.
why: Round-2 grounding: two passes independently showed clause-level failure — the key-derived rule does NOT refuse the symlink-into-another-repository case, it mints a relative label anchored to a tree the memo never names. Re-derived and captured live (F22) and the mechanism is narrowed with a second, capture-time-available condition rather than the sentence being reworded.

prop: The residual anchor hazard — an observation taken directly against a genuinely different repository, where key, spelling and world_root all agree and the relative label is nonetheless anchored to a tree the memo never names — cannot be closed at capture time, but it can be made visible at check time without touching render output. `worldstate::tree_report` already walks every fact's extent entries collecting `world_root`, is defined at src/worldstate.rs:249 and called from exactly one place, the check driver at src/lib.rs:175, and already feeds a human-owed section of `check`. Extending it to report the set of distinct `world_root`s a memo's relative-marked labels are anchored to, and to name that root explicitly, reads nothing the snapshot does not already carry. It is not a render change: `snapshot::check` byte-compares the memo against a re-render of its snapshot, and `check`'s own printed rows are not part of that comparison, so this guard cannot redden `[provenance-drift]` on any committed memo. That places the answer to "relative to what, and is it one tree?" inside this ticket rather than deferring it to TET-43.

why: The clause about `snapshot::check` byte-comparing memo against re-render rests on F8, which was not cited.

The third condition is not decoration: without it a `look` through a symlink from inside the shipping repository into a different repository satisfies the first two and mints a bare relative label anchored to the other repository, which resolves in the shipping tree to a different file. Within that guarantee fall plain single-file labels and, per C27, a whole-search label's root and the in-repo paths its exclusion note enumerates. It makes no promise about author-typed text — claim propositions and fact notes alike, the latter rendering in the Facts table's own Note column — about `proc:` command lines, or about an entry whose world marker degraded to `no-git-worktree`, which stays absolute even when the file is physically inside the shipping checkout; the committed corpus already contains such an entry, under this worktree's own `.git`. (2) An evidence ledger inherits that guarantee for `predicate.extent[]` and explicitly keeps `predicate.world[].root` absolute, because it is the identity of the tree, not a citation into it. (3) A snapshot keeps every key that is a path absolute, and canonical except where `search_key` deliberately adopts the world marker's `--show-toplevel` spelling for a whole-search root — because `key` is what `ExtentEntry::censuses` compares against `world_root` — and stores the same relativized labels the memo renders. prop: An absolute label is what the surfaces produce in practice, but it is not enforced anywhere, and the design must not rest on a structural impossibility that does not exist. prop: Clause (1)'s "otherwise" branch cannot promise an absolute label, and its caller-spelling condition has no stated meaning for a relative spelling. Nothing between the caller's argv and the stored label absolutizes anything, so a caller-relative spelling survives into the label verbatim. Captured on the release build `tetel 0.1.0` at HEAD 01b140c, in a scratch tree holding a real one-file git repository `outer` beside a sibling directory in no repository: from that sibling, `tetel look ../outer/x.txt` mints key `<s>/outer/x.txt`, world_root `<s>/outer` — a real repository with the key strictly under it — and label `../outer/x.txt`. From inside `outer`, `tetel look x.txt` mints the same key and world_root with the label `x.txt`, which is byte-identical in shape to the root-relative label clause (1) would mint. Two consequences follow. First, the condition must say what a relative spelling is compared against — the rule this design adopts is a lexical join onto the process's working directory, without following symlinks, which admits the two fixture arms above (both resolve under their own world_root) and still refuses the symlink-into-another-repository case, whose spelling is already absolute and outside the answering root. Second, even so the residue is not absolute, so the guarantee must be stated as "relative to the root when the three conditions hold, and otherwise exactly as the caller spelled it".

Absolutizing a caller-relative spelling at capture is out of TET-42's scope, and is carried as a named risk rather than promised in the contract. The only absolutization available is a join onto the process's working directory — exactly what `fn resolved` (src/mcp.rs:186) does for the MCP handlers that use it, returning `std::env::current_dir().map(|d| d.join(p))` for a relative path rather than refusing it. Its own doc states the cost of applying that to a stored label: "The server cannot know the caller's working directory, so a relative path silently means something different to each side", and "Nothing here changes *which* file is opened — that was always resolved against this process's directory". So over MCP the promise "absolute otherwise" would be kept in letter by storing a path anchored to a server directory the caller cannot see or set, trading one label a reader cannot resolve for another. It also reaches observations this design otherwise does not touch: every relative-spelled `look`, including the two CLI pin tests that drive `look f.txt` with the sandbox repository as cwd, would have its stored label rewritten, and since `mint` hashes the label and not the key, every one of their pins would move for a reason unrelated to root-relativization. The contract TET-42 should adopt, per artifact: (1) a rendered memo guarantees that every tool-generated extent label is spelled relative to a repository root when three conditions hold together on the entry — its `world_root` resolved to a real repository, its canonical key sits at or strictly under that root, and the path as the caller spelled it also lies under that same root, compared after resolving a relative spelling lexically against the process's working directory and without following symlinks — and is otherwise left exactly as the caller spelled it. Both halves of that sentence are load-bearing. The third condition is not decoration: without it a `look` through a symlink from inside the shipping repository into a different repository satisfies the first two and mints a bare relative label anchored to the other repository, which resolves in the shipping tree to a different file; and it needs the resolution rule stated, because "the path as the caller spelled it lies under that root" has no truth value for a relative spelling until it is said what that spelling is resolved against. The "otherwise" branch promises the caller's spelling and not an absolute path, because nothing at capture absolutizes a relative one and neither authoring surface enforces absoluteness: measured on the release build, `look ../outer/x.txt` from a directory in no repository lands in that branch carrying exactly the label `../outer/x.txt`. What distinguishes a root-relative label from a caller's own relative spelling is therefore the marker, not the shape of the string. Within the guarantee fall plain single-file labels and, per C27, a whole-search label's root and the in-repo paths its exclusion note enumerates. It makes no promise about author-typed text — claim propositions and fact notes alike, the latter rendering in the Facts table's own Note column — about `proc:` command lines, or about an entry whose world marker degraded to `no-git-worktree`, which stays absolute even when the file is physically inside the shipping checkout; the committed corpus already contains such an entry, under this worktree's own `.git`. (3) A snapshot keeps every key that is a path absolute, and canonical except where `search_key` deliberately adopts the world marker's `--show-toplevel` spelling for a whole-search root — because `key` is what `ExtentEntry::censuses` compares against `world_root` — and stores the same relativized labels the memo renders. Clauses (1) through (3) are deliverable because labels and keys are independent fields, the label is built at capture from a `world_root` and a caller spelling both already on the pending entry, and the only render sites print stored labels verbatim; clause (4) is deliverable because `tree_report` already reads every entry's `world_root` at a call site inside the check driver.

prop: Condition three does not close the escape into a different repository when the symlink is traversed by the WORKING DIRECTORY rather than by the spelled path, and nothing at capture can close it. The rule uses the PHYSICAL working directory — `std::env::current_dir()`, the getcwd(3) the operating system reports — and the contract says which one, because "the process's working directory" has two readings and they classify this case oppositely. Physical is chosen for two reasons, not one. It is the only working directory the capture path can obtain: src/observe.rs consults none at all, and the whole crate reads one at exactly two sites, src/worldstate.rs:209 and src/mcp.rs:191, both `std::env::current_dir()`. And the alternative is not a better answer but a worse one: a logical `PWD` is maintained by shells on `cd` and by nothing else, so a process whose directory was `<s>/otherrepo` was measured seeing `PWD=/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel`, a third directory inherited stale from a parent — and over MCP, where agents author, `fn resolved`'s own doc comment (src/mcp.rs:170-200) states the server cannot know the caller's working directory at all. Under the physical reading the resolved spelling of a bare `x.txt` is `<s>/otherrepo/x.txt`, which carries the answering root as a literal prefix, so all three conditions hold and the bare label is minted. That is the ceiling of what capture can see rather than a defect in the wording: getcwd hands over a directory the kernel has already resolved, so the untraversed spelling of where the caller was standing exists nowhere in the process. The case is routed to clause (4)'s check-time report of distinct anchoring roots, the same place the nested-repository case goes, and the contract states this rather than implying condition three closes it. It is the worse of the two residues: a nested repository needs a submodule or a vendored checkout, while this needs only a `cd` through a symlink, the label it mints is shape-identical to a sound one, and clause (4) reports that a memo's labels are anchored to more than one root without saying which label is wrong.

The contract TET-42 should adopt, per artifact: (1) a rendered memo guarantees that every tool-generated extent label is spelled relative to a repository root when three conditions hold together on the entry — its `world_root` resolved to a real repository, its canonical key sits at or strictly under that root, and the path as the caller spelled it also lies under that same root — and is otherwise left exactly as the caller spelled it. Both halves of that sentence are load-bearing. The third condition is not decoration: without it a `look` through a symlink from inside the shipping repository into a different repository satisfies the first two and mints a bare relative label anchored to the other repository, which resolves in the shipping tree to a different file. And it needs its resolution rule stated in terms that admit one reading only, because "the path as the caller spelled it lies under that root" has no truth value for a relative spelling until it is said what that spelling is resolved against. The rule adopted, stated so that it cannot be read the other way: an absolute spelling is the literal string the caller typed; a relative spelling is the process's PHYSICAL working directory — `std::env::current_dir()`, the getcwd(3) the operating system reports, in which the kernel has already resolved every symlink — and that string concatenated with a single separator between them, with no `..` component collapsed, no symlink followed and no filesystem consulted; and the condition holds exactly when the resulting string carries the root followed by a separator as a literal prefix. prop: The anchor should be `world_root` (the observation's own `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), not the memo's directory. `world_root` is resolved at capture from the observed path and is already on the pending entry, whereas the memo's location does not exist until `render --out` — an anchor a capture-time mechanism cannot consult. Empirically the two coincide for the whole committed corpus: across all committed snapshots every extent entry's world_root is either this repository or the degraded NO_GIT marker, and no committed memo cites a fact taken against a different repository than the one it ships in. The choice is not free, and it fails in three shapes rather than one. A repository elsewhere on the machine, observed directly. A repository nested beneath the shipping worktree — a submodule, a vendored checkout — because `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` answers with the *innermost* repository: constructed and captured, an observation of `outer/vendor/sub/src/a.rs` derives the label `src/a.rs`, which resolves against the outer worktree to a different file that exists there, contents "OUTER FILE" against the observed "NESTED FILE". And, the most ordinary of the three, a symlink from inside the shipping worktree into a separate repository elsewhere: captured on the release build, `look outer/link/x.txt` where `outer/link` points at `otherrepo` mints world_root `.../otherrepo` and key `.../otherrepo/x.txt`, because `Session::for_path` canonicalizes the containing directory before asking git. The third shape is closed at capture by C19's caller-spelling condition only when the escaping symlink lies in the SPELLED path, since only then does the spelled path fail to lie under the answering root. The same shape reached by a working directory standing on that symlink — `cd outer/link` and then `look x.txt`, captured on the release build with key and world_root in `otherrepo` — is not closed, because getcwd hands the capture path a directory in which the kernel has already resolved the symlink away. All three are what C29's check-time report on distinct anchoring roots exists to surface. Nothing in this repository reaches any of them today: `git submodule status` prints nothing and no nested `.git` exists below the root.

prop: The relative label must be derived from the canonicalized key against the entry's own `world_root`, AND minted only when the caller's own spelling lies under that same `world_root`. Two conditions, because each defeats a different attack and neither defeats both. Deriving from the key rather than by stripping a prefix off the caller's spelling defeats the escape into a non-repository: `look <repo>/link/x.txt` through a symlink out of the tree, and `look <repo>/../outside/x.txt`, both carry a key that is not under the repository root, so no strip applies and the label stays absolute, where a textual strip would have minted `link/x.txt`. But the key-derived rule alone does not defeat the escape into a *different* repository, and that case is reachable with an ordinary symlink. Constructed and captured on the release build: `look .../outer/link/x.txt`, where `outer/link` is a committed symlink to a separate repository `otherrepo`, mints key `.../otherrepo/x.txt` and `world_root` `.../otherrepo`, because `Session::for_path` canonicalizes the containing directory before asking git. The key is strictly under that entry's own world_root, so a key-only rule mints the relative label `x.txt` — not absolute and not a refusal — and `x.txt` resolves in the shipping worktree `outer` to a file that exists there holding "OUTER x" against the observed "OTHER FILE". The second condition catches that spelling: the caller's spelling `.../outer/link/x.txt` does not lie under `world_root` `.../otherrepo`, whereas in the control observation `look .../outer/README.md` the key, the label and the world_root all agree. What it does not catch is the same escape reached without spelling the symlink at all: from a working directory spelled `.../outer/link`, `look x.txt` mints the same key and world_root, and because the working directory the process can read is the already-resolved `.../otherrepo`, the caller's spelling resolves under the answering root and all three conditions hold. The second condition is therefore a defence against an escaping symlink in the spelled path, not against the escape as such; the working-directory form is left to the check-time report. Both operands of the condition are already on the pending entry for an absolute spelling, so it adds a second comparison rather than a new mechanism, and it costs nothing on any observation that did not traverse out of the tree the caller was working in.

prop: The residual anchor hazard — an entry whose relative label is correctly derived and nonetheless anchored to a tree the memo never names — cannot be closed at capture time, but it can be made visible at check time without touching render output. It has three shapes, not one: an observation taken directly against a genuinely different repository, an observation of a file inside a repository nested beneath the shipping worktree, and an observation issued from a working directory that reached another repository through a symlink, where key, spelling and world_root all agree because getcwd resolved the symlink away before capture saw it. prop: A partial capture-time guard against the symlinked-working-directory escape DOES exist, and this design rejects it on grounds other than impossibility — which is a correction, because two earlier drafts asserted it was unavailable. The measurement, re-derived in a scratch tree `<s>` holding two real repositories with `<s>/outer/link` a committed symlink to `<s>/otherrepo`: after a shell `cd <s>/outer/link`, an external child process inherits `PWD=<s>/outer/link` — precisely the untraversed spelling the design claimed existed nowhere in the process — while `getcwd()` reports `<s>/otherrepo`, and `realpath(PWD) == getcwd()` is True, so the spelling is not merely present but verifiable against the physical directory without trusting the shell. A guard that reads `PWD`, uses it as the caller's working directory ONLY when `realpath(PWD) == getcwd()`, and otherwise falls back to `getcwd()`, therefore refuses the escaping capture — `<s>/outer/link` does not lie under the answering root `<s>/otherrepo` — while accepting the control `cd <s>/outer` unchanged, where `PWD == getcwd() == <s>/outer` lies under its own answering root. Every degraded arm the design already measured survives and is what makes the validity test necessary rather than what makes the guard impossible: with the `chdir` performed by the process rather than by a shell, `PWD` stayed at the shell's own directory while `getcwd()` had moved, so `realpath(PWD) == getcwd()` is False and the guard falls back; under `env -i` `PWD` is absent entirely while `getcwd()` still answers. So the honest statement is that the guard is PARTIAL, not unavailable. It is nonetheless not adopted, and the reason is where it helps rather than whether it works: it closes the shape only where `PWD` is the caller's own, which is the CLI invoked from an interactive shell. Over MCP — through which agents author, and which is therefore the surface the hazard is most likely to be reached on — the server process's `PWD` is not the caller's at all, the same fact `fn resolved`'s doc comment states when it says the server cannot know the caller's working directory. The guard therefore helps precisely the surface on which the hazard is least reachable and is inert on the one where it is most reachable, so the design routes all three residual shapes to clause (4)'s check-time report uniformly rather than closing one of them on one surface and leaving the report to explain why the coverage is asymmetric. What must not be said, and what earlier drafts did say, is that no capture-time rule can close it.

The rule uses the PHYSICAL working directory — `std::env::current_dir()`, the getcwd(3) the operating system reports — and the contract says which one, because "the process's working directory" has two readings and they classify this case oppositely. Physical is chosen for two reasons. It is the working directory the capture path actually reads: `src/observe.rs` consults none at all, and the whole crate reads one at exactly two sites, src/worldstate.rs:209 and src/mcp.rs:191, both `std::env::current_dir()`. Under the physical reading the resolved spelling of a bare `x.txt` is `<s>/otherrepo/x.txt`, which carries the answering root as a literal prefix, so all three conditions hold and the bare label is minted. prop: The contract TET-42 should adopt, per artifact: (1) a rendered memo guarantees that every tool-generated extent label is spelled relative to a repository root when three conditions hold together on the entry — its `world_root` resolved to a real repository, its canonical key sits at or strictly under that root, and the path as the caller spelled it also lies under that same root — and is otherwise left exactly as the caller spelled it. Both halves of that sentence are load-bearing. The third condition is not decoration: without it a `look` through a symlink from inside the shipping repository into a different repository satisfies the first two and mints a bare relative label anchored to the other repository, which resolves in the shipping tree to a different file. And it needs its resolution rule stated in terms that admit one reading only, because "the path as the caller spelled it lies under that root" has no truth value for a relative spelling until it is said what that spelling is resolved against. The rule adopted, stated so that it cannot be read the other way: an absolute spelling is the literal string the caller typed; a relative spelling is the process's PHYSICAL working directory — `std::env::current_dir()`, the getcwd(3) the operating system reports, in which the kernel has already resolved every symlink — and that string concatenated with a single separator between them, with no `..` component collapsed, no symlink followed and no filesystem consulted; and the condition holds exactly when the resulting string carries the root followed by a separator as a literal prefix. Physical rather than logical is not a shrug, and the reason is not that a logical `PWD` is unobtainable. Physical is what the capture path reads today — the crate reads a working directory at exactly two sites, both `std::env::current_dir()`, and `src/observe.rs` reads none — while a logical `PWD` is a shell convention that arrives stale or foreign whenever the process was not started by a shell's `cd`: measured stale at `/Volumes/SSD/Documents/lonic/tetel` for a process that had performed its own `chdir` elsewhere, absent entirely under `env -i`, and not the caller's directory at all over MCP, whose own doc says the server cannot know it. `PWD` is nonetheless, in the shell case, exactly the caller's untraversed spelling and verifiably so, which is why this contract rejects a `PWD`-reading guard on the ground of where it helps rather than on the ground that it cannot exist. Captured on the release build in a scratch tree `<s>` holding two real repositories: with the working directory inside the shipping repository `outer`, `tetel look ../otherrepo/x.txt` mints `world_root` `<s>/otherrepo` and key `<s>/otherrepo/x.txt`, so under the collapsing reading the spelling normalizes to exactly the key, all three conditions hold, and a bare `x.txt` is minted anchored to `otherrepo` — which resolves in `outer` to a different file that exists there, "OUTER x" against the observed "OTHER FILE". That is the failure condition three was introduced to prevent, reached through condition three itself. What is stable is the 489, its per-directory decomposition, and the property asserted of it. The two are complementary rather than overlapping, and they sum: 93+113, 48+51 and 75+38 give C27's 206, 99 and 113. prop: The residual anchor hazard — an entry whose relative label is correctly derived and nonetheless anchored to a tree the memo never names — is not closed at capture time, but it can be made visible at check time without touching render output. It has three shapes, not one: an observation taken directly against a genuinely different repository, an observation of a file inside a repository nested beneath the shipping worktree, and an observation issued from a working directory that reached another repository through a symlink, where key, spelling and world_root all agree because getcwd resolved the symlink away before capture saw it. Capture time cannot separate the first two from a legitimate observation, because capture time does not know which memo this fact will end up in. The third is partially separable, and this claim no longer says otherwise: after a shell `cd` through the escaping symlink the process inherits a `PWD` naming the untraversed directory, with `realpath(PWD) == getcwd()` confirming it is a live alias rather than a stale inheritance, so a capture-time guard trusting `PWD` only under that equality would refuse that observation and accept the control unchanged. It is left unclosed for a stated reason rather than an impossible one — `PWD` is the caller's own only on the CLI, and over MCP, the surface agents author on, it is the server's — so all three shapes still reach this report on the surface that matters most. `worldstate::tree_report` already walks every fact's extent entries collecting `world_root` and is defined at src/worldstate.rs:249. A grep of the whole of src/ for the name returns that definition and seven call sites, and the split is worth stating because this memo makes the same distinction for `PendingEntry` and `ExtentEntry` elsewhere: exactly one is production, the check driver at src/lib.rs:175, and the other six — src/worldstate.rs:322, 343, 354, 363, 370 and 376 — are inside that file's own `#[cfg(test)]` module, whose single attribute sits at line 293. One production caller is what bounds the blast radius. The function already feeds a human-owed section of `check`. Extending it to report the set of distinct `world_root`s a memo's relative-marked labels are anchored to, and to name each root explicitly, reads nothing the snapshot does not already carry. It is not a render change: `snapshot::check` byte-compares the memo against a re-render of its snapshot, and `check`'s own printed rows are not part of that comparison, so this guard cannot redden `[provenance-drift]` on any committed memo. That places the answer to "relative to what, and is it one tree?" inside this ticket rather than deferring it to TET-43. What it does not place inside this ticket is a fix, and it is a report a human must read rather than a check that fails. More than one root tells a reader something is wrong without telling them which label is the wrong one; and where every label in a memo is anchored to one and the same wrong tree there is nothing anomalous to detect at all — the report names that root, and only a reader who knows which repository the memo ships in can tell that it is the wrong one.
why: Round 6, answering both grounding passes. (a) "called from exactly one place, the check driver at src/lib.rs:175" is a production-only census: a grep of src/ for the name returns the definition plus seven call sites, six of them inside worldstate.rs's own #[cfg(test)] module, whose attribute is at line 293 (F38). The production/test split is now stated, matching the standard C20 already sets for PendingEntry and ExtentEntry. (b) "Capture time cannot separate any of them from a legitimate observation" is true of the first two shapes but over-claims on the third: a PWD-reading guard validated against getcwd does separate it on the CLI (F36). Narrowed to the first two, with the third stated as partially separable and unclosed for a stated reason rather than an impossible one. The blast-radius and no-drift conclusions are unchanged.
